summary: MiniMax H3 on images as one-frame clips: the picture stream only (the model's silent audio stream is left out of the loss), on top of a de-distillation training adapter.
notes: H3 is guidance-distilled: sample at CFG 1, as its released sampler does (CFG doubles the time and overcooks).

Training straight on a distilled model spends the LoRA undoing the distillation (validation loss starts ~3x higher, worst at high noise). Put a de-distillation adapter under it: Network → Training adapter. circlestone-labs' image adapter suits image datasets; it's applied while training only, never in samples or the saved LoRA.
Video and stereo audio are denoised together; an image trains as a one-frame clip with silence beside it, and only the picture counts toward the loss.
One image per step: the model takes batch size 1. Use gradient accumulation for a bigger batch.
The int8 build (~21 GB) mostly stays in VRAM and trains about twice as fast as the bf16 one (~40 GB, streamed): ~1.3 s/step at 1024² on a 5090.
Training shift 3 (sampling uses 12) spends more steps on detail: likeness and faces.
Sides are multiples of 32 (16x VAE, 2x2 patches); 64-step buckets satisfy that.
The text encoder is a 32B vision-language model: captions and sample prompts are encoded once, cached, and it's never loaded again for that dataset.

Adapters go on blocks 20-49 only (Fizgig's default, measured there to keep the model's motion and layout and reach likeness sooner): the backward stops at block 20, so steps are quicker. Clear Network → Blocks to train all 50.

Speed defaults from a one-change-at-a-time ablation against a known-good audio run (Oct 2026): int8 forward + W8A8 backward + blocks 20-49 keep samples, beat and loss in line with it at about half the step time (6.0 -> 3.1 s). TREAD distorted both picture and audio on clip-only datasets, so it stays off here; turn on Clip stills before trying it.
